title: Dominic and the Uniform
premise: In the river town of Vellmouth, where Jude Ravensworth cuts type matrices beside their father, the winter bridge closes and seals the town inside a gathering uprising. When soldiers of the Provisional Directorate seize the print shop to control what can be printed, Jude discovers that whoever sets the type sets the truth. Hiding the shop's second press in the flooded cellars, they print an underground chronicle documenting the Directorate's massacres, racing the thaw — when the bridge reopens, the victors' historians arrive, and every loose page becomes evidence or ash. The book ends at the breaking ice: Jude rows the chronicle's plates across the river as the bridge opens, trading the shop, their father's freedom, and nearly their life for a record that outlives the regime.
about_author: Edmund Pemberton is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about ordinary tradespeople caught in extraordinary politics.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Jude Ravensworth's POV. Establishes the print shop, the craft of cutting type, and Jude's conviction that history happens elsewhere. Their father dismisses talk of unrest as tavern noise. Emotional beat: comfortable complacency on the edge of change.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Town criers announce the seasonal closure of the only bridge; no one leaves until the ice breaks. Jude watches the last ferry go and feels the town contract around them. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as inconvenience.

chapters.title: Strangers at the Door
chapters.summary: Officers of the Provisional Directorate requisition the shop 'for public information.' Captain Aldous Verrek inspects the presses and orders all output pre-approved. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: humiliation and the first flicker of defiance.

chapters.title: What the Type Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude finds evidence in old jobbing work — a suppressed broadsheet from an earlier purge — proving the Directorate repeats its own crimes. Father warns them to burn it. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the past pressing its face against the present.

chapters.title: The Cellar Press
chapters.summary: Jude and apprentice Wren Corliss discover the shop's decommissioned second press beneath floodwater in the cellars. They begin restoring it in secret. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: conspiratorial thrill, first true alliance.

chapters.title: First Impression
chapters.summary: The underground chronicle's first issue prints by candlelight: names of the disappeared from the mill district. Distribution through the fishwives' market. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Verrek's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Verrek visits socially, probing Jude with unsettling charm; he quotes back a phrase suspiciously close to the chronicle's language. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: paranoia — is it coincidence or bait?

chapters.title: The Fishwife's Network
chapters.summary: POV: Maren Ostler, fishwife and distributor, showing the risk borne by those who carry the pages. A courier is detained and questioned. Emotional beat: solidarity shadowed by cost; the network tightens its discipline.

chapters.title: Father's Hands
chapters.summary: Jude's father is forced to cut commemorative type praising the Directorate's 'restoration of order.' His craftsmanship becomes complicity. POV: the father. Emotional beat: shame, and his silent decision to mis-cut key letters as sabotage.

chapters.title: Snow Over the Square
chapters.summary: A public execution of mill strikers; the official broadsheet lies about it, and the chronicle tells the truth within hours. The town begins to believe the cellar press over the Directorate. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief hardened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Someone in the network talks; a safehouse is raided. Maren suspects a newcomer named Pell. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: trust fracturing; the movement learns secrecy the hard way.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Type Case
chapters.summary: Jude and Wren argue over whether to print names of suspected informants — justice outside the law vs. mob rule. They choose restraint, printing procedures instead. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: moral maturation; power examined.

chapters.title: Verrek Ascendant
chapters.summary: POV: Verrek. He burns books he deems seditious in the square and promotes himself on the chaos, revealing his ambition to write the town's history himself. Emotional beat: the antagonist's cold clarity; readers see corruption as method.

chapters.title: The Raid That Missed
chapters.summary: Soldiers search the shop while the cellar press runs below, muffled by the rising river's sound. Jude's father stalls Verrek upstairs with typographic pedantry. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: near-discovery; breathless suspense.

chapters.title: Pell's Choice
chapters.summary: The informant Pell, wracked by guilt after a prisoner dies under interrogation, comes to Jude seeking absolution and offers proof of Verrek's forged casualty ledgers. POV: Pell. Emotional beat: redemption sought, forgiveness withheld but used.

chapters.title: Ice Groaning
chapters.summary: Thaw approaches early; the Directorate announces historians will arrive by the first barge to compile the 'official record.' The chronicle must be finished and moved before then. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: The Last Set
chapters.summary: A marathon printing session; father's sabotaged letters are discovered by Verrek's clerks, and he is arrested. Jude must choose: rescue him or protect the plates. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: devastating trade-off; father, from custody, signals them to run.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Maren organizes a diversionary fire at the customs house; Pell surrenders himself to draw patrols away, knowing he won't return. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: sacrifice without spectacle; justice as collective act.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the River
chapters.summary: Climax. As the ice cracks, Jude rows the plates and full chronicle across the swollen river under gunfire while Wren holds the cellar press as decoy. Verrek pursues to the bank. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: terror, grief, and unbreakable will.

chapters.title: The Historians Arrive
chapters.summary: The victors' historians land to find the shop emptied, the press drowned, and copies already circulating in three neighboring provinces. Verrek's forged ledgers surface alongside them. POV: Verrek. Emotional beat: the corrupt discovering memory outranks power.

chapters.title: Typeset in Permanence
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the father is released in the regime's collapse; the chronicle is formally entered as evidence. Jude returns to cutting type — but now for a free press. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: weary, earned peace.

chapters.title: The Second Proof
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Jude and Wren reprint the chronicle for the archive, correcting one name they'd once gotten wrong — justice as ongoing revision. The final line is set by hand. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: humility before history; memory kept alive by craft.
